harmonicFunction: C (I) - Tonic chord establishing the comforting home base
Em (iii) - Mediant minor chord adding warmth, gentleness, and emotional depth
F (IV) - Subdominant chord introducing melodic hope and lift
G (V) - Dominant chord propelling resolution smoothly back to C
Bb (bVII) - Borrowed Mixolydian flat-seven chord providing the signature bridge emotional surge

techniques.name: Gentle Acoustic Finger-and-Pick Strum
techniques.description: Delicate, nuanced acoustic strumming at a slow 82 BPM, highlighting individual bass notes on beat 1 with warm brush strums on treble strings

sequence: Establish a tender 82 BPM ballad tempo
Pick the individual bass string on beat 1 (5th string for C and Am, 6th string for G and Em)
Brush gently downward across strings 3, 2, and 1 on beat 2
Maintain relaxed wrist motion throughout the verse
tips: Play with a warm, thin-to-medium pick for a soft acoustic texture
If full barre F is difficult, open Fmaj7 (X-X-3-2-1-0) sounds wonderfully lush in this context
Let open strings ring freely without abrupt muting

techniques.name: Borrowed Flat-Seventh (bVII) Barre Transition
techniques.description: Navigating the unexpected Bb major chord in the bridge, sliding from 1st-fret A-shape barre (Bb) to standard F and resolving to open C

notes: Bb chord: X-1-3-3-3-1 (A-shape barre at 1st fret)
sequence: Shift from open C cleanly into the 1st-fret Bb barre chord
Hold the Bb for 2 full beats with warm resonance
Move into standard F for 2 beats
Resolve home to ringing open C major
tips: Barre the 1st fret firmly with your index finger for the Bb chord
Use the ring finger or pinky across strings 4, 3, and 2
This chord change is the emotional climax of the song — strum it with conviction

sections.name: Intro
sections.description: Neil Finn introduces the song alone on an acoustic guitar with a quiet, tender cycle through C, Em, F, and G.
notes: Quiet, reverent acoustic strumming at 82 BPM
Notice the gentle shift from C to Em
Establish an intimate campfire atmosphere

sections.name: Verse
sections.description: The poignant storytelling verse pairs intimate acoustic strums with Finn's searching vocal melody.
sections.progression: C - Em - F - G - C - Em - F - G
notes: Keep the volume gentle and supportive
Smooth finger transitions between C and Em
Let the F chord sustain with emotional warmth

sections.name: Chorus
sections.description: The heartfelt singalong chorus shifts focus to the relative minor Am before resolving warmly through F and G into C.
sections.progression: Am - F - G - C - Am - F - G - C
notes: Increase strumming dynamic for the chorus hook
Sing the soaring vocal melody along with the acoustic pulse
Clean resolution into open C major
sections.exerciseLabel: Better Be Home Soon Chorus Cadence

sections.name: Bridge (Modal Mixture)
sections.description: The emotional turning point: an unexpected Bb major chord enters with powerful vulnerability, resolving through F into C.
sections.progression: Bb - F - C - Bb - F - G
notes: Strike the Bb barre chord with emotional intensity
Listen to the modal shift from bright major to soulful rock ballad
G builds tension before the final triumphant chorus

sections.name: Scale Practice Exercise
sections.description: Scale run demonstrating the natural B note alongside the borrowed Bb flat-seven note used in the bridge.
notes: Notice how the Bb note on string 3 fret 3 creates the signature modal color
Alternate picking across strings 5 to 1
Connect scale positions directly with the open C and Bb shapes

beginner.title: Master the Verse & Chorus Open Chords
steps: Learn open C, Em, G, and Am chord shapes
Use open Fmaj7 (X-X-3-2-1-0) as a stepping stone to full barre F
Practice the C - Em - F - G verse progression at 70 BPM
Sing along with the famous chorus hook

intermediate.title: Master the Bridge Bb Barre Chord
steps: Learn the 1st-fret A-shape Bb barre chord (X-1-3-3-3-1)
Practice the bridge progression: Bb → F → C with a metronome at 82 BPM
Work on smooth transitions into full barre F in both verse and chorus
Play through the entire song structure without dropping the rhythm

advanced.title: Soulful Vocal & Acoustic Performance
steps: Deliver Neil Finn's tender vocal phrasing with authentic emotional weight
Add subtle walking bass transitions between C and Em (C → B → E)
Incorporate light thumb-picked bass notes on the verses
Lead an unforgettable Australasian campfire singalong

commonMistakes: Strumming too loudly on the verses — this ballad relies on tender, intimate dynamics
Stumbling on the quick shift to Bb in the bridge — drill the C to Bb change in isolation
Playing too fast — 82 BPM is slow, measured, and soulful
Muting the high E string on the Bb and F chords
practiceRoutine: 2 minutes: Open chord finger warm-up across C, Em, F, G, and Am
5 minutes: Verse progression (C - Em - F - G) at 82 BPM with steady down-up strumming
5 minutes: Isolated drill of the bridge (Bb → F → C) transition
5 minutes: Chorus flow (Am - F - G - C) focusing on vocal delivery
5 minutes: Full song play-through from intro to final chord
metronomeWork: Set metronome to 70 BPM to master the bridge chord changes
Advance to 82 BPM once the Bb transition is smooth and clean
Practice setting clicks on beats 2 and 4 to develop natural ballad sway
Verify you do not rush the tempo during the emotional chorus
